newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada had budget surplus in Dec, reserve unneeded.
newsitem.headline: Canada had budget surplus in Dec, reserve unneeded.

text.p: The federal government ran a C$2.19 billion budget surplus in December and is doing so well this fiscal year that its contingency reserve will not be used, the Finance Department said on Tuesday.
For the fiscal year to date, April through December, the budget deficit was only C$5.93 billion, down from C$19.11 billion over the same period a year earlier, it said in its monthly Fiscal Monitor.

Economists caution that January through March are usually the worse fiscal months as tax refunds go out and that there are also end-of-year accounting adjustments that have historically added C$3 billion to C$6.4 billion more to the deficit. But progress on the deficit is still far better than budgeted.
"As indicated in the 1997 budget, the deficit for the year as a whole is now estimated at no more than C$19.0 billion -- at least C$5.3 billion below target," the Fiscal Monitor said.

Lehman Brothers economist Michael Gregory told Reuters that based on past year-end adjustments and the progress made so far, the actual outcome could be even billions of dollars better than the new target.

"It looks like somewhere between C$14.2 billion and C$17.6 billion, based on the actual flows for the first nine months of the year and the typical kinds of year-end adjustments that are usually made," he said.
Lower than expected interest rates have yielded public debt charges that are expected to be C$2.3 billion less than projected in the March 1996 budget, the Fiscal Monitor said.

"This, in combination with strict control over program spending, has meant that the contingency reserve will not be required in 1996-97, the third consecutive year in which this has occurred," it said. The reserve was worth C$2.5 billion.
The following Finance Department figures are in billions of Canadian dollars. Positive numbers indicate a net source of funds, negative a net requirement.
